## Firewall allowlist refresh

Long runs no longer lose GitHub partway through. Until now the egress firewall resolved
each allowlisted hostname once, at boot. GitHub's DNS rotates `github.com`,
`api.github.com` and `codeload.github.com` through Azure-hosted addresses that its
published ranges do not list, so a later lookup could hand `git` or `gh` an address no
rule allowed, and the connection timed out. The image now keeps the allowlist current
for the whole run. The change is additive: there is no image contract change from v0.5.0
(contract 3).

### Added

- `agent-firewall-refresh` is a root process that the agent user cannot signal,
  started with none of the run's secret variables in its environment. It re-resolves
  the same allowlisted hostnames every `AGENT_FIREWALL_REFRESH` seconds (default `60`)
  and adds a rule for each new public address. It applies the same private-range
  filter as boot and never removes a rule. A connection to a new address can wait up to
  one interval for its rule, which `git`'s connect timeout (about two minutes) outlasts;
  a client with a shorter one can still fail in that window. Each addition logs one
  line, for example
  `agent-firewall-refresh: allowed 20.250.119.72 for api.github.com`.
- `AGENT_FIREWALL_REFRESH=0` turns the refresher off and restores the v0.5.0 behaviour.
  The refresher never runs in proxy mode or with `AGENT_FIREWALL=0`.
- `AGENT_FIREWALL_RULE_CAP` (default `2048`) bounds the number of address rules. At the
  cap, the refresher stops adding rules and logs one warning.
- GitHub's published ranges are re-fetched every ten refreshes, conditionally on the
  stored ETag. A failed or rate-limited fetch keeps the current rules.
- `docker exec -u root <container> agent-egress-check` lists every address the
  allowlist resolves to right now and whether a rule covers it. It exits `1` if any
  address is uncovered.
- Boot logs one line with the number of addresses from each source (resolved,
  `allow-ranges.d`, live `api.github.com/meta`) and whether the meta fetch succeeded or
  was rate-limited. `AGENT_VERBOSE=1` also logs each resolved address.

### Changed

- The shipped GitHub range snapshot (`allow-ranges.d/github`) is refreshed from
  `api.github.com/meta`: 64 → 78 ranges, none removed.

### Internal

- The address filter, resolution, CIDR matching and the meta fetch move into
  `lib/firewall.sh`, which boot, the refresher and the check share.
- `smoke.sh` case 11 runs as the agent in a real container. It checks that the
  refresher runs as root, that the agent cannot kill it or run `iptables`, and that
  `example.com` stays blocked after refreshes.

### Upgrade

Use `claude-v0.6.0`. No launcher change is needed. Set `AGENT_FIREWALL_REFRESH` only to
change the interval or turn the refresher off.
